scope: HEIF/HEIC browser-native, decoder, bounded-memory, security, and distribution-licensing feasibility
decision: Do not publish HEIF/HEIC input or output routes in the current build. A conditional HEIC decode prototype is technically plausible, but no candidate currently satisfies the combined stable-browser, fixed-memory, security-maintenance, legal-clearance, reproducibility, fidelity, and acceptance-evidence requirements.

productionBrowserProbe.interpretation: Chrome has no complete browser-native HEIF/HEIC ImageDecoder path. This machine does expose HEVC VideoDecoder configurations, so a separate HEIF parser plus the browser codec is a possible conditional design, not a complete or portable conversion route.

focusedRegression.command: npx playwright test tests/browser/privacy-offline.spec.ts --grep functional browser capability probes

containerLibrary.name: libheif
containerLibrary.readerApi: heif_context_read_from_reader exposes seek/read/range callbacks and is suitable for a custom bounded bridge.
containerLibrary.securityLimits: The library exposes configurable image, item, tile, entity, metadata, and allocation limits; a production wrapper would have to lower and enforce them rather than disable them.

browserCodecDesign.codecAvailability: runtime-dependent and not guaranteed by the WebCodecs specification
observedCopies: A bounded HEVC item is exposed from Wasm memory to EncodedVideoChunk.
The plugin allocates a complete decoded VideoFrame-sized JavaScript Uint8Array (or Canvas ImageData for formats with no copyable native format).
Decoded planes are copied again into libheif-owned Wasm image planes before color conversion/output.
boundedPrototypeRequirements: Reject before decode above a fixed 8-megapixel, 8192-pixel-edge, compressed-item-byte, item-count, tile-count, derivation-depth, metadata-byte, and expansion-ratio budget.
Compile only the HEIF container and WebCodecs HEVC decoder path: no libde265, encoders, dynamic plugins, uncompressed codec, JPEG 2000, VVC, or experimental container APIs.
Replace the stock growing heap with explicit equal INITIAL_MEMORY and MAXIMUM_MEMORY values and fail before allocation pressure crosses the profile budget.
Use the existing bounded synchronous file bridge for reader callbacks, a dedicated disposable worker, strict cancellation/time limits, and incremental direct PNG output with one pending write.
Probe the exact hvc1/hev1 configuration derived from the file before conversion and show an unsupported-browser result when it is unavailable.
Independently validate dimensions, alpha, orientation/transforms, bit depth, color profile/CICP, EXIF/XMP behavior, grids, thumbnails, and malformed-input cleanup before any route is public.

reasons: The upstream script enables ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH and therefore does not provide the required fixed Wasm maximum.
The WebCodecs backend is explicitly experimental and adds Asyncify.
The script defaults to bundled libde265 1.0.15, while the current security release is 1.1.2; this project would disable libde265 rather than ship that default.
The upstream JavaScript-facing path is not the project's bounded random-access reader and direct incremental destination abstraction.

localToolchain.note: This is not itself a rejection reason; any accepted engine would use the existing pinned no-Docker Emscripten CI pattern.

securityAssessment.upstreamPolicy: Only the latest libheif release receives fixes; there is no maintained LTS branch and libheif/libde265 have one independent maintainer with no security team.
securityAssessment.currentChurn: The official policy records 37 libheif advisories from January through August 2026, including 3 critical and 13 high, and six primarily security-driven releases.
securityAssessment.latestRelease: libheif 1.23.3 was four days old at this audit and fixed one critical, three high, and several medium/low issues plus hardening defects. libde265 1.1.2 was three days old and fixed two use-after-free paths plus parser hardening, although libde265 is not required by the preferred browser-codec design.
securityAssessment.wasmBoundary: Wasm containment reduces native-process compromise risk, but parser bugs can still corrupt output, expose bytes retained inside the worker, exhaust the fixed heap/CPU budget, deadlock, or crash a conversion. Dedicated-worker termination and strict limits are necessary but not yet sufficient evidence.
securityAssessment.shippingResult: Do not add an untrusted-file parser while the required narrow build, adversarial corpus, update policy, and acceptance suite are absent.

licensingAssessment.openSourceLicense: libheif is LGPL-3.0-or-later and would require corresponding notices/source/relinking compliance for a distributed Wasm build.
licensingAssessment.codecPatentStatus: The open-source license does not establish HEVC patent clearance. Access Advance states that its pool licenses HEVC decoders and encoders in consumer products, including software; Via LA also operates an HEVC patent portfolio program.
licensingAssessment.projectClearance: No project-owned legal analysis, patent-pool license, or written clearance for offering HEVC still-image decoding was found.
licensingAssessment.shippingResult: Withhold the route pending explicit qualified legal clearance, consistently with the project's AMR-WB policy. Browser-provided decoding is the preferred technical design but is not treated here as automatic patent clearance.

revisitConditions: Document qualified legal clearance for the exact browser-provided HEVC decode and any HEIF encode design and target jurisdictions.
Pin a then-current libheif release/commit and establish an actionable security-update policy with no known unpatched applicable advisory.
Build a no-Docker, HEVC-only, no-plugin, non-experimental-surface Wasm wrapper with fixed initial/maximum memory and the bounded reader/direct writer architecture above.

Pass genuine production-browser success, corrupt/adversarial, unsupported-codec, cancellation, timeout, write-failure, cleanup, privacy/offline, independent fidelity, three-run process-tree memory, and cross-browser capability gates.
Keep the route capability-gated; never fall back to a full-file buffer, server conversion, native helper, or extension rename.
